bull_bear.body:
- Established engineering and project execution capabilities across thermal, nuclear and electrical infrastructure, preserved through the downturn
- Qualified position in nuclear power EPC — executing Main Plant Electrical Systems and C&I packages for NPCIL at Kudankulam, Kakrapar (KAPP 3&4) and Rawatbhata (RAPP 7&8)
- Manufacturing Division with established capability to design and manufacture equipment for power, oil & gas, process and infrastructure sectors
- Long-standing customer relationships with NTPC, NUPPL, APGENCO and NPCIL evidenced by ongoing multi-package contracts
- Experienced engineering workforce redeployable into an asset-light Engineering Services model with lower capital requirements than EPC
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Going-concern uncertainty — The statutory auditors drew attention by way of Emphasis of Matter to material uncertainty relating to going concern, alongside claims on the NUPPL Ghatampur and NTTPS Vijayawada contracts and the assignment of dues by certain banks to NARCL. This is the risk that subsumes all others: the Company's continued existence depends on the debt resolution succeeding.
- Liquidity and working-capital constraint from NPA classification of borrowings — Borrowings were classified as Non-Performing Assets by the lending consortium in prior years, and the resulting prolonged liquidity constraint has directly impaired project execution, procurement of materials, mobilisation of manpower and overall operational efficiency. It also forced the Company to stop accepting new Balance of Plant orders, which is the proximate cause of the revenue decline.
- Execution dependence on debt resolution with NARCL — A substantial portion of the financial debt has been assigned to the National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited, but the restructuring is only proposed, not concluded, and settlement discussions were still ongoing. Borrowings from Axis Bank, ICICI Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank remain outside the NARCL assignment, so a comprehensive resolution requires more than one counterparty to agree.
- Negative and deteriorating net worth — The MD&A states net worth deteriorated further during the year, remaining deeply negative, on account of reduction in turnover and increased operating costs. Negative net worth constrains bonding, bid qualification and the ability to win new EPC work independently of the lenders' position.
- Insolvency and claim petitions from vendors, sub-contractors and a lender — The Board's Report tabulates numerous insolvency and claim petitions filed against the Company for unpaid civil work, services and material supply, plus a working-capital claim by a bank, each currently stayed by the Andhra Pradesh High Court. The protection is procedural: an adverse outcome on the stays would expose the Company to admission of insolvency proceedings.
- Structural decline and customer concentration in the conventional thermal power sector — Management cites challenges in the thermal power sector in India and global markets as the reason a shift out of current business segments is critical. Lower order inflows in conventional thermal directly depressed manufacturing activity and capacity utilisation, and the remaining order book is concentrated in a small number of public-sector counterparties (NUPPL, APGENCO, NPCIL, NTPC).
- Order-book run-off with no replenishment — Nearly every disclosed project is beyond 90% complete and no new BoP orders are being accepted, so the executable backlog is being consumed without replacement. The Board notes under Conservation of Energy that most projects are near completion and there are no new orders — a structural revenue cliff unless the diversification and Engineering Services verticals scale.
- Receivable realisation and counterparty payment delays — Delays in customer payments are cited as a continuing drag alongside increased input costs and supply-chain challenges, and disrupted billing milestones impaired revenue recognition. Debtor days on the Company's own disclosure remain extremely elevated, tying up the working capital the business does not have.
- Contract and project-execution risk inherent to the EPC model — The MD&A Risk Management section notes the business spans design, manufacturing at factories and project sites, civil and mechanical construction, erection and commissioning, managed through a documented Standard Operating Systems and Procedures framework with an experienced contract-specialist team reviewing all customer and vendor contractual documents to ensure contractual risks are understood and documented.
- Group reporting and governance control weaknesses — The consolidated financial results carried a Qualified Opinion because consolidation relied entirely on un-audited, management-certified provisional financials of the material subsidiaries, leaving final audit adjustments unverified. The Secretarial Audit further flagged late website filing of subsidiary financials, subsidiary board minutes not placed before the holding-company board, failure to appoint Independent Directors on material unlisted subsidiary boards, and delayed payments to micro and small vendors under the MSMED Act.

business.body: The Company executes engineering, procurement and construction contracts for power and infrastructure customers, covering Balance of Plant packages for thermal stations, and Main Plant Electrical Systems, switchyard and C&I packages for nuclear power projects. A Manufacturing Business (Product Business Division) designs and manufactures equipment and spares for the power, oil & gas, petrochemical and process industries in domestic and international markets. During FY 2025-26 the Company added an asset-light Engineering Services vertical providing engineering design, detailed engineering, technical documentation and project engineering support to international customers.

outlook.body:
- Prioritise execution and completion of ongoing legacy projects only, accepting no new Balance of Plant (BoP) orders while working capital remains constrained (MD&A Business Overview, routed into the profile bundle of this same annual report).
- Complete the debt resolution with the National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited (NARCL), to whom a substantial portion of the consortium bank debt was assigned, to rationalise principal and accrued interest and rebuild networth; borrowings from Axis Bank, ICICI Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank remain with those lenders.
- Shift out of the shrinking conventional thermal BoP business into adjacent sectors identified as medium-term growth drivers: water and water treatment solutions, electricity transmission & distribution, transport infrastructure (metro, railways, highways), civil construction, project exports, oil & gas equipment, and engineering services.
- Build the new asset-light Engineering Services vertical — engineering design, detailed engineering, technical documentation and project engineering support for international customers — leveraging the existing engineering workforce with lower capital intensity than EPC.
- Remain a selective participant in thermal generation while directing order-seeking effort at nuclear power projects and power transmission, where the Company holds executing credentials with NPCIL.
- Expand geographic reach of the capital goods / manufacturing business into international markets and broaden the product portfolio into niche engineering products with higher value addition.
- Continue cost optimisation, effective resource utilisation and operational-efficiency improvement across business verticals; retain critical technical and managerial talent through the downturn.
- Raise capital to strengthen the financial position — shareholders approved doubling the Authorised Share Capital to Rs 200 crore by postal ballot on 5 July 2026 — and pursue further measures to reduce other liabilities.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: BGR Energy is not undertaking capacity expansion in FY 2025-26; its footprint activity is the completion of a legacy EPC order book under severe working-capital constraint, with no new Balance of Plant orders accepted. On the 3 x 660 MW Ghatampur Thermal Power Project for NUPPL, Unit I attained commercial operation in December 2024 and Unit II in November 2025, while Unit III is scheduled for completion in the first quarter of FY 2026-27; as on 31 March 2026 physical progress was 91.2% and financial progress 88.8%. The 1 x 800 MW NTTPS project of APGENCO has been in commercial operation since December 2023, with ash handling and Stage-V effluent treatment works completed and balance coal handling plant and railway marshalling yard works poised for completion by September 2026, the project having progressed beyond 90% of scope. For NPCIL's 2 x 1000 MW Light Water Reactor project at Kudankulam the Company executes the Electrical and C&I packages: the 220 KV GIS was recently taken into service and work on the 400 KV GIS is progressing, with the electrical job slated for completion in September 2026 and balance C&I items scheduled for delivery by 31 March 2027. The Main Plant Electrical Systems Package for Kakrapar Atomic Power Project (KAPP) 3 & 4 has been completed, taken over by the customer and granted operational acceptance. At NPCIL's Rawatbhata Atomic Power Project (RAPP) Units 7 & 8, Unit 7 is complete with operational acceptance obtained and Unit 8 works are in progress, 98.5% complete against a scheduled completion of March 2026. The 220kV Switchyard Extension at Tarapur, Maharashtra is more than 94% complete with pre-commissioning under way. At NTPC's 2 x 600 MW Tanda Thermal Power Plant Stage-II, both units are commissioned and operational with more than 96% of the electrical equipment supply and erection job completed. In the Manufacturing Business (Product Business Division), lower thermal-sector order inflows and constrained working capital reduced manufacturing activity and capacity utilisation; the division completed 23 product supply and spares orders during the year. Forward expansion intent is directed at new verticals rather than plant capacity — an asset-light Engineering Services business with lower capital requirements than conventional EPC, and diversification into water treatment, transmission & distribution, transport infrastructure, civil construction, project exports and oil & gas equipment. Under Conservation of Energy the Board states that as most projects are near completion and there are no new orders, no major initiative has been taken.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management states the financial restructuring will facilitate faster execution of ongoing projects, improve operational efficiency and rebuild confidence among customers, vendors, lenders and other stakeholders, enabling the Company to pursue new business opportunities in its core engineering and infrastructure segments.
- Management believes the Engineering Services business will emerge as an important contributor to long-term growth, generating stable service-based revenue streams and improving operational flexibility and business diversification.
- Demand backdrop cited is challenges in the thermal power sector in India and in global markets, which is what prompted the identified need to shift out of current business segments.
- Adjacent sectors are framed as growth drivers because they attract public and private investment, and management considers the Company's track record and competencies leverageable into these emerging industrial, core and infrastructure sectors.
- Lower order inflows in the conventional thermal power sector, combined with the constrained working capital position, depressed manufacturing activity and capacity utilisation during the year.
- Revenue recognition was constrained by disruptions in procurement, mobilisation of project resources and execution schedules, which impacted billing milestones.
- Conservation of energy initiatives were not undertaken because most projects are near completion and there are no new orders.
- No new Balance of Plant (BoP) orders were accepted during FY 2025-26; management consciously adopted a conservative approach towards new order acquisition, particularly in the conventional BoP business.
- An additional order of Rs 70.0 Cr was received in the current financial year on the NPCIL Kudankulam Electrical package.
- The Manufacturing Division completed 23 product supply and spares orders during the year for customers across the power, oil & gas, petrochemical and process industries, both domestic and international.
- The Company secured engineering services assignments from international customers during the year, its first step into the global engineering services market.
- Ongoing execution portfolio spans the 3 x 660 MW Ghatampur (NUPPL), 1 x 800 MW NTTPS (APGENCO), NPCIL Kudankulam 2 x 1000 MW, NPCIL RAPP 7 & 8, the Tarapur 220kV switchyard extension and NTPC's 2 x 600 MW Tanda Stage-II packages, most of which are beyond 90% complete.

open.item: The Main Plant Electrical Systems Package at NPCIL's RAPP Units 7 & 8 is scheduled for completion by March 2026, with 98.5% of works completed and Unit 7 already granted operational acceptance.

Unit III of the 3 x 660 MW Ghatampur Thermal Power Project (NUPPL) is scheduled to be completed in the first quarter of FY 2026-27, with physical progress at 91.2% and financial progress at 88.8% as on 31 March 2026.
The Electrical package at NPCIL's Kudankulam 2 x 1000 MW Light Water Reactor project is slated for completion in September 2026, with 73.63% of contract value delivered.

A Special Resolution at the 40th AGM (22 September 2026) proposes shifting the registered office from one state to another, from the current registered office at Pannamgadu Industrial Estate, Tirupathi District, Andhra Pradesh.
Balance works on the Coal handling plant and Railway marshalling yard at APGENCO's 1 x 800 MW NTTPS project are poised for completion by September 2026.
The Electrical package for NPCIL's 2 x 1000 MW Light Water Reactor project at Kudankulam is slated for completion in September 2026.
Balance items on the Kudankulam C&I package are scheduled to be delivered by 31 March 2027, with approximately 51.54% of contract value delivered so far.
Balance items on the C&I package for NPCIL's Kudankulam project are scheduled to be delivered by 31 March 2027.

The Company will diversify into water and water treatment, T&D, transport infrastructure, civil construction, project exports, oil & gas equipment and engineering services as medium-term growth drivers.

Balance installation and commissioning of electrical auxiliaries at NTPC's 2 x 600 MW Tanda Thermal Power Plant Stage-II are under progress, with more than 96% of the job completed and both units commissioned and operational.
In capital goods / manufacturing, the Company has taken measures to expand geographical market reach in international markets by identifying key opportunities for expanding the product portfolio.
The Company has taken steps to ensure future consolidated financial statements are based on audited (not management-certified provisional) financial statements of its subsidiaries and joint venture.
Henceforth the minutes of the Board Meetings of the unlisted subsidiaries will be placed at all Board Meetings of the holding Company, addressing the Regulation 24(3) lapse.
The Company has initiated the process for appointment of Independent Directors on the Boards of its material unlisted subsidiaries and will ensure compliance with Regulation 24 of SEBI LODR.
The Company is in discussions with NARCL for a mutual settlement of outstanding dues, with the proposed restructuring expected to reduce principal and accrued interest and improve networth.

The Company will continue as a significant market player in thermal generation, being selective in order booking, while focusing on seeking orders from nuclear power projects and power transmission activities.

Management flags that prolonged liquidity constraints from the NPA classification of its borrowings continue to impair project execution, procurement, manpower mobilisation and overall operational efficiency.

The proposed restructuring with NARCL, to whom a substantial portion of the Company's financial debt was assigned, is expected to rationalise liabilities through an overall reduction in debt including principal and accrued interest, strengthening the financial position and improving networth.

The Company intends to further strengthen the asset-light Engineering Services business by expanding engineering capabilities, adopting advanced digital engineering tools and exploring additional domestic and international opportunities.

The Company intends to diversify into adjacent sectors — water and water treatment solutions, electricity transmission & distribution, transport infrastructure (metro, railways, highways), civil construction, project exports, oil & gas equipment, and engineering services — as medium-term growth drivers.

For NPCIL's 2 x 1000 MW Light Water Reactor project at Kudankulam the Company executes the Electrical and C&I packages: the 220 KV GIS was recently taken into service and work on the 400 KV GIS is progressing, with the electrical job slated for completion in September 2026 and balance C&I items scheduled for delivery by 31 March 2027. risks.note: The statutory auditors drew attention by way of Emphasis of Matter to material uncertainty relating to going concern, alongside claims on the NUPPL Ghatampur and NTTPS Vijayawada contracts and the assignment of dues by certain banks to NARCL. This is the risk that subsumes all others: the Company's continued existence depends on the debt resolution succeeding.

risks.risk: Liquidity and working-capital constraint from NPA classification of borrowings
risks.note: Borrowings were classified as Non-Performing Assets by the lending consortium in prior years, and the resulting prolonged liquidity constraint has directly impaired project execution, procurement of materials, mobilisation of manpower and overall operational efficiency. It also forced the Company to stop accepting new Balance of Plant orders, which is the proximate cause of the revenue decline.

risks.risk: Execution dependence on debt resolution with NARCL
risks.note: A substantial portion of the financial debt has been assigned to the National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited, but the restructuring is only proposed, not concluded, and settlement discussions were still ongoing. Borrowings from Axis Bank, ICICI Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank remain outside the NARCL assignment, so a comprehensive resolution requires more than one counterparty to agree.

The MD&A states net worth deteriorated further during the year, remaining deeply negative, on account of reduction in turnover and increased operating costs. Negative net worth constrains bonding, bid qualification and the ability to win new EPC work independently of the lenders' position.

risks.risk: Insolvency and claim petitions from vendors, sub-contractors and a lender
risks.note: The Board's Report tabulates numerous insolvency and claim petitions filed against the Company for unpaid civil work, services and material supply, plus a working-capital claim by a bank, each currently stayed by the Andhra Pradesh High Court. The protection is procedural: an adverse outcome on the stays would expose the Company to admission of insolvency proceedings.

risks.risk: Structural decline and customer concentration in the conventional thermal power sector
risks.note: Management cites challenges in the thermal power sector in India and global markets as the reason a shift out of current business segments is critical. Lower order inflows in conventional thermal directly depressed manufacturing activity and capacity utilisation, and the remaining order book is concentrated in a small number of public-sector counterparties (NUPPL, APGENCO, NPCIL, NTPC).

Nearly every disclosed project is beyond 90% complete and no new BoP orders are being accepted, so the executable backlog is being consumed without replacement. The Board notes under Conservation of Energy that most projects are near completion and there are no new orders — a structural revenue cliff unless the diversification and Engineering Services verticals scale.

risks.risk: Receivable realisation and counterparty payment delays
risks.note: Delays in customer payments are cited as a continuing drag alongside increased input costs and supply-chain challenges, and disrupted billing milestones impaired revenue recognition. Debtor days on the Company's own disclosure remain extremely elevated, tying up the working capital the business does not have.

risks.risk: Contract and project-execution risk inherent to the EPC model
risks.note: The MD&A Risk Management section notes the business spans design, manufacturing at factories and project sites, civil and mechanical construction, erection and commissioning, managed through a documented Standard Operating Systems and Procedures framework with an experienced contract-specialist team reviewing all customer and vendor contractual documents to ensure contractual risks are understood and documented.

risks.risk: Group reporting and governance control weaknesses
risks.note: The consolidated financial results carried a Qualified Opinion because consolidation relied entirely on un-audited, management-certified provisional financials of the material subsidiaries, leaving final audit adjustments unverified. The Secretarial Audit further flagged late website filing of subsidiary financials, subsidiary board minutes not placed before the holding-company board, failure to appoint Independent Directors on material unlisted subsidiary boards, and delayed payments to micro and small vendors under the MSMED Act.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management states the financial restructuring will facilitate faster execution of ongoing projects, improve operational efficiency and rebuild confidence among customers, vendors, lenders and other stakeholders, enabling the Company to pursue new business opportunities in its core engineering and infrastructure segments.
- Management believes the Engineering Services business will emerge as an important contributor to long-term growth, generating stable service-based revenue streams and improving operational flexibility and business diversification.
- Demand backdrop cited is challenges in the thermal power sector in India and in global markets, which is what prompted the identified need to shift out of current business segments.
- Adjacent sectors are framed as growth drivers because they attract public and private investment, and management considers the Company's track record and competencies leverageable into these emerging industrial, core and infrastructure sectors.
- Lower order inflows in the conventional thermal power sector, combined with the constrained working capital position, depressed manufacturing activity and capacity utilisation during the year.
- Revenue recognition was constrained by disruptions in procurement, mobilisation of project resources and execution schedules, which impacted billing milestones.
- Conservation of energy initiatives were not undertaken because most projects are near completion and there are no new orders.
- No new Balance of Plant (BoP) orders were accepted during FY 2025-26; management consciously adopted a conservative approach towards new order acquisition, particularly in the conventional BoP business.
- An additional order of Rs 70.0 Cr was received in the current financial year on the NPCIL Kudankulam Electrical package.
- The Manufacturing Division completed 23 product supply and spares orders during the year for customers across the power, oil & gas, petrochemical and process industries, both domestic and international.
- The Company secured engineering services assignments from international customers during the year, its first step into the global engineering services market.
- Ongoing execution portfolio spans the 3 x 660 MW Ghatampur (NUPPL), 1 x 800 MW NTTPS (APGENCO), NPCIL Kudankulam 2 x 1000 MW, NPCIL RAPP 7 & 8, the Tarapur 220kV switchyard extension and NTPC's 2 x 600 MW Tanda Stage-II packages, most of which are beyond 90% complete.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Prioritise execution and completion of ongoing legacy projects only, accepting no new Balance of Plant (BoP) orders while working capital remains constrained (MD&A Business Overview, routed into the profile bundle of this same annual report).
- Complete the debt resolution with the National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited (NARCL), to whom a substantial portion of the consortium bank debt was assigned, to rationalise principal and accrued interest and rebuild networth; borrowings from Axis Bank, ICICI Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank remain with those lenders.
- Shift out of the shrinking conventional thermal BoP business into adjacent sectors identified as medium-term growth drivers: water and water treatment solutions, electricity transmission & distribution, transport infrastructure (metro, railways, highways), civil construction, project exports, oil & gas equipment, and engineering services.
- Build the new asset-light Engineering Services vertical — engineering design, detailed engineering, technical documentation and project engineering support for international customers — leveraging the existing engineering workforce with lower capital intensity than EPC.
- Remain a selective participant in thermal generation while directing order-seeking effort at nuclear power projects and power transmission, where the Company holds executing credentials with NPCIL.
- Expand geographic reach of the capital goods / manufacturing business into international markets and broaden the product portfolio into niche engineering products with higher value addition.
- Continue cost optimisation, effective resource utilisation and operational-efficiency improvement across business verticals; retain critical technical and managerial talent through the downturn.
- Raise capital to strengthen the financial position — shareholders approved doubling the Authorised Share Capital to Rs 200 crore by postal ballot on 5 July 2026 — and pursue further measures to reduce other liabilities.
